sections.h2: Where is a Connecticut quitclaim deed recorded?
sections.html:
A deed goes on the land records of the town where the land lies. Section 47-10 says no conveyance is effectual to hold land against anyone except the grantor and the grantor's heirs unless it is recorded in the records of the town in which the land lies.

Connecticut has 169 municipalities, and the recording office is the clerk in the town, not a county recorder. A house in Hamden is recorded in Hamden, even though the state also groups towns into historical counties and planning regions. If the parcel sits in more than one town, ask each clerk how they want the deed handled.

An unrecorded quitclaim is a risk to both sides. The grantee may hold a paper that does not protect them against a later buyer or lender, and the grantor may still look like the owner of record when a lien or tax bill is issued.

sections.h2: What must a Connecticut deed contain to be valid?
sections.html:
Under section 47-5, a conveyance of land must be in writing, signed by the grantor, acknowledged by the grantor, and attested by two witnesses. Those formalities apply to a quitclaim deed the same way they apply to any other deed.

  • In writing, signed by the grantor or by an agent whose power of attorney was itself executed, acknowledged and witnessed as the statute requires.
  • A corporation, limited liability company or partnership signs through a duly authorized person.
  • Acknowledged as the grantor's free act and deed.
  • Attested to by two witnesses with their own hands.
  • The current mailing address of the grantee must be included.

If an agent signs under a power of attorney, section 47-10 also requires that power of attorney to be recorded with the deed, unless it is already recorded in that town and the deed refers to it. Families who use a power of attorney for a parent's house often miss that second step.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a quitclaim deed in Connecticut?
sections.html:
The fee is set by section 7-34a: ten dollars for the first page and five dollars for each additional page. The statute names a quitclaim deed among the statutory-form documents, on a form conforming to section 47-36c and titled "statutory form" in the heading, that carry the same ten and five dollar charges.

A few add-ons can raise the bill. The statute lists these extras:

SituationAdded charge under 7-34a
Deed lacks the grantee's current mailing address$5 on top of the regular fee
Names not printed or typed beneath signatures, witnesses and notary$1 on top of the regular fee
Document requiring data sent to the Office of Policy and Management under 10-261b$2 on top of the regular fee
Copy of a recorded document$1 per page; certifying a copy is $2

Other charges can apply to a deed, including the conveyance tax discussed below, so ask the clerk for a total before you mail anything.

sections.h2: Is there a tax on a quitclaim deed?
sections.html:
Possibly. The conveyance tax in section 12-494 applies to a deed or other instrument that conveys real property when the consideration equals or exceeds $2,000. The tax follows the consideration, not the name of the deed form. A quitclaim with a real price attached is taxed like any other sale deed.

The base rates are three-quarters of one percent to the state and one-quarter of one percent to the municipality. Residential value above $800,000 and non-residential use carry higher state rates. On a $250,000 transfer for value, the base charge is about $2,500 in all.

Section 12-499 explains where the money goes: the town clerk remits the state portion to the Commissioner of Revenue Services, and the municipal portion becomes general revenue of the town.

sections.h2: When is a quitclaim deed exempt from the conveyance tax?
sections.html:
Several listed transfers are exempt under section 12-498, and these come up most often with family quitclaims.

  • Deeds between spouses.
  • Deeds where the consideration is less than $2,000.
  • Transfers that change only the identity or form of ownership, with no change in beneficial ownership.
  • Deeds in lieu of foreclosure that transfer the transferor's principal residence.
  • Deeds securing a debt, and deeds releasing property held as security.
  • Deeds made under certain superior court decrees named in the statute.

An exemption does not remove the deed's other costs, and it does not erase the property tax. It also does not tell you whether a transfer is wise. A gift or a no-price deed within the family can still raise questions about an existing mortgage and about the owner's own plans. Those are matters for an attorney, and the statutes cited here do not settle them.

sections.h2: Does a quitclaim deed fix a tax, lien or title problem?
sections.html:
Not by itself, and none of the statutes cited here say otherwise. A recorded tax levy, a mortgage or an unpaid municipal bill stays on the property until it is paid or released. The grantee takes the house in whatever condition the title is in.

Property tax is billed against the parcel. Under section 12-111, a person to whom title has been transferred since the assessment date can appeal the assessment, which shows that the tax system expects ownership to change hands while a year's bill is open. A new owner should find out about the October 1 assessment and any unpaid installments before closing on a quitclaim.

If the reason for the quitclaim is a divorce, an estate or a dispute among heirs, the court file or probate record may control what the deed can say. A title company can search the land records and tell you what is open.

sections.h2: Can I sell a house after receiving it by quitclaim?
sections.html:
Yes, provided the deed was properly signed, witnessed, acknowledged and recorded, and the title searches cleanly. A buyer's title company will look at how the seller took title, and a gap in recording or a missing power of attorney will surface at that point.

Sellers who got a house this way often face the same issues: back taxes, repairs, a co-owner who has not signed, or heirs who disagree. Cash buyers who purchase as-is regularly deal with these files. The first step is a clean copy of the recorded deed and the current tax bill, which together show who owns the house and what is owed on it.

If the buyer is paying in cash, closing speed depends mostly on how fast the clerk's office returns the recorded deed and how soon the payoff figures arrive. Sellers who live far from the property should ask the title company how to arrange the signing so the acknowledgment and the two witnesses meet section 47-5.

For a quick reference, three documents carry most of the weight at closing: the recorded deed, the tax collector's payoff statement and any power of attorney that was used.

faqs.q: Where do I record a quitclaim deed in Connecticut?
faqs.a: With the town clerk in the town where the property is located. Section 47-10 makes recording in that town's land records what protects the grantee against third parties.

faqs.q: How many witnesses does a Connecticut deed need?
faqs.a: Two. Section 47-5 requires the deed to be in writing, signed, acknowledged by the grantor and attested to by two witnesses, and to include the grantee's current mailing address.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a Connecticut quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: Ten dollars for the first page and five dollars for each additional page under section 7-34a, plus any add-on charges the statute lists, such as $5 when the grantee's mailing address is missing.

faqs.q: Do I pay conveyance tax on a quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: If the consideration is $2,000 or more and no exemption applies, yes. The base rate is 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the municipality. Deeds between spouses are exempt.

faqs.q: Is a power of attorney recorded with the deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 47-10 requires the power of attorney to be recorded with the deed unless it is already recorded in that town and the deed refers to it.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed remove a tax lien?
faqs.a: No. A deed moves ownership and does not discharge a lien or an unpaid tax. Ask the tax collector and a title company what is open before you sign.
